8. The decisive experiment

The next useful test is a full 100 mm head, not another isolated tip test.

Initial stopping gate

Use 32 blind patches: eight from each of the four manufacturing lots.

Require:

Lower-confidence initial clamp ≥575 N.
Measured individual foot force–motion behavior.
Clean, observable release and reset.
At least one 24-hour reference hold per surface family retaining ≥540 N.
No excessive damage, hidden support or active-bank replacement.

If the construction cannot pass that gate, the full endurance campaign should stop.

The 500-acceptance campaign

Use:

300 first-attempt blind patches, 75 per lot.
100 accepted repetitions on one designated concrete patch.
100 accepted repetitions on one designated clay patch.
Additional prospectively selected attempts if needed to reach 500 acceptances, with all failures counted.
Ten distributed 24-hour holds covering material, lot, normal/shear/bending endpoints and mixed directions.
Short declared holds for the remaining cycles.

The remaining cycles must not be described as 500 demonstrated full-day services.

Require at least 90% observed acceptance per lot. For statistical context, 279 successes from 300 trials gives an approximately 90.1% one-sided 95% lower binomial bound; 270/300 does not establish a population rate of 90%.

Twenty concealed physical challenges cover dust, ineffective banks, imperfect restoration, actuator/lock faults and adverse pose or local surface conditions. The controller sees instrument observations, not challenge labels.

Numerical measurement gates
Measurement	Required commissioning target
Installed wrench	Error ≤2 N and ≤0.1 N·m
Port motion	Uncertainty ≤0.02 mm and ≤0.03°
Total clamp	Lower-confidence uncertainty ≤5 N
Surface loss	Depth uncertainty ≤15 µm
Fragment sizing	Uncertainty ≤0.05 mm
Energy	Common module meter; separate robot and research-utility meters

These are requirements to establish through calibration, not supplied instrument performance.

Measure all tip working zones, each pad, spring force curves and locking features through life. A complete pad or bank replacement fails that head’s active-stock contract. A 12 × 12 × 1 mm pad contains approximately 163 mg at the candidate density, leaving only about 8.1 mg permissible loss per pad.

The proof excursions themselves also consume contact life and wall stock; they are not free qualification.

Paid
